text:
Last night's Integration Debt Night at Kestrelmoor's Flatiron office was one of the more useful rooms I've been in this year. About 60 of us showed up to hear how teams are dealing with the unglamorous work of connecting systems.

A few things stuck with me:

Priya Raman-Holt (VP Platform, Tallowbrook) said her team maintains 140 partner integrations with just three engineers. How? "We stopped building connectors one by one and started publishing a spec. Partners build to it now."

Marcus Feldane (founder, Quillary) argued that agent pilots fail at the integration seam, not at the model. His team's rule: wire up data access before choosing a model.

That landed. Marcus asked for a show of hands on who'd had an agent pilot stall on data access. About 40 of the 60 raised one.

The best moment was a real disagreement. Priya thinks partners should own their connectors. Marcus thinks the platform has to own them or quality drifts. I left without a clear winner, and I think both are right depending on how much control you need over the end experience.

My takeaway: before the next AI pilot, ask who owns the plumbing and whether it's written down as a spec.

Thanks to the Kestrelmoor team for hosting.

Where has integration debt slowed you down?
